newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs firm as Nikkei weakens.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs firm as Nikkei weakens.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were off their highs but remained relatively firm in late trade on Thursday following a drop in Tokyo stocks on the back of the yen's strength.
"Everything's been focused on the forex market today. When the dollar/yen came off sharply, the immediate reaction was to sell the Nikkei and buy Euroyen," a dealer at a European futures house said.

Dealers said the yen's strength should have given a further lift to the Japanese interest rate market but strong selling pressure on the upper end capped December Euroyen at 98.95 while June JGBs were unable to climb above 124.19.
December Euroyen stood at 98.92 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 98.91. June JGBs settled at 123.70 against their previous 123.73.
The dollar was quoted at 115.45/55 at 1115 GMT after falling to a low of 114.70 yen earlier.
"Maybe the market felt the move in the yen was not warranted and it would come back down so there was not much point in buying Euroyen up too much," a trader with an Asian house said.
He said the December contract faced resistance at 98.96/97 while June JGBs looked toppish around 124.20/50.

Eurodollar futures failed to extend their gains after an overnight rise on weaker than expected U.S. wholesale price data for April. December ended at 93.690 against its IMM close at 93.700 on light volume of 6,170 lots.
Dealers said the market was awaiting the release of the U.S. Consumer Price Index at 1230 GMT.
